example: AI is becoming increasingly capable, so it can handle a wider range of tasks.
note: Part 3：AI 是否会取代工作

meaning: 一些工作可以被自动化
example: Some jobs can be automated, especially those involving predictable procedures.
note: automate / automated

example: Unlike human workers, machines can work around the clock.
note: around the clock = 24小时不停

example: AI can process large amounts of data without getting tired.
note: 可与 work around the clock 连用

example: AI is particularly suitable for routine and repetitive tasks.
note: routine and repetitive 连读练习

front: take over certain jobs or tasks
example: In the future, AI may take over certain jobs or tasks.
note: take over = 接管、接替

example: Businesses use AI to become more efficient and productive.
note: efficient 强调效率；productive 强调产出

meaning: 对雇主来说更具成本效益
example: Automation can be cost-effective for employers in the long run.
note: cost-effective = 划算的

example: One reason companies adopt AI is to reduce labour costs.
note: 英式拼写 labour

example: Greater efficiency may help companies increase profits.
note: profit 常用复数 profits

meaning: 需要人的判断力和同理心
example: Medical and teaching jobs require human judgment and empathy.
note: 反方核心理由

example: People-facing professions are much harder to replace.
note: harder to replace 比 cannot replace 更客观

example: AI cannot fully understand human emotions, at least for now.
note: 用于限制观点，表达更严谨

front: jobs related to the AI industry
meaning: 与 AI 行业相关的工作
example: More jobs related to the AI industry are likely to appear.
note: Part 3：AI 是否创造就业

example: Digital skills will become increasingly important in the workplace.
note: 趋势类高频表达

example: Software engineers are needed to develop AI systems.
note: develop systems

example: Skilled workers will be required to maintain AI systems.
note: maintain /meɪnˈteɪn/

example: Human employees still need to monitor AI systems.
note: monitor 作动词

meaning: 监督 AI 如何运行
example: Specialists should oversee how AI operates in sensitive fields.
note: oversee = supervise

example: AI can still make mistakes, so human supervision is necessary.
note: 可自然引出人工监督

front: break down from time to time
example: Even advanced machines can break down from time to time.
note: break down = 出故障

example: Technicians are employed to maintain and repair systems.
note: 两个并列动词

front: make sure something is working properly
example: Human technicians make sure the technology is working properly.
note: 口语化万能表达

front: the demand for these jobs is likely to increase
meaning: 对这些工作的需求可能会上升
example: As AI spreads, the demand for these jobs is likely to increase.
note: the demand for + 名词

example: AI development will create opportunities in data management.
note: 工作领域名词

example: System maintenance will remain an important area of employment.
note: maintenance /ˈmeɪntənəns/

example: Ethical oversight is necessary when AI affects people's lives.
note: 适用于隐私、公平、医疗等话题

example: Although AI may remove some jobs, it can also create new opportunities.
note: 让步转折句核心搭配

front: have a responsibility to do something
example: Governments have a responsibility to support displaced workers.
note: responsibility 后接 to do

front: have an obligation to do something
example: Governments have an obligation to protect vulnerable citizens.
note: 比 responsibility 语气更强

front: be supposed to serve the public
example: After all, governments are supposed to serve the public.
note: 适合补充政府责任理由

example: Public funds should be used to support people in need.
note: people in need = 困难人群

example: Unemployed workers may struggle to support themselves financially.
note: financially 作副词

example: People need practical skills to make a living in a changing economy.
note: 自然口语表达

example: Temporary aid can help families meet their basic needs.
note: meet needs = 满足需求

example: People who suddenly lose their jobs may be under severe financial pressure.
note: under pressure 固定搭配

example: Supporting unemployed people can help maintain social stability.
note: 政府措施的社会层面结果

example: Financial support may reduce social problems caused by unemployment.
note: caused by 作后置修饰

example: Without support, a small number of people may turn to crime.
note: 避免绝对化，用 may / a small number of

example: Governments should consider individual circumstances before offering aid.
note: circumstances 常用复数

example: Authorities should provide targeted support instead of using one solution for everyone.
note: targeted = 有针对性的

example: Temporary financial assistance can give workers time to retrain.
note: assistance 不可数

example: Governments could offer retraining programs in growing industries.
note: 英式也可拼 programmes

front: help people transition into new jobs
meaning: 帮助人们过渡到新的工作
example: Training can help people transition into new jobs more smoothly.
note: transition into = 过渡到
